sources.title: unicode-org.github.io
sources.version_or_date: Live user guide; includes later MessageFormat 2.0 references
sources.sections_read: Overview, MessageFormat and Complex Argument Types.
sources.confirmed: The guide treats a message as a translatable unit with variable placeholders and locale-dependent plural or keyword-based select branches. It explains why concatenating sentence fragments restricts translators.
sources.limits: This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C20.json.

sources.title: Boost.Locale 1.55.0
sources.version_or_date: Boost 1.55.0; release date corroborated by the official release page as 2013-11-11
sources.sections_read: Introduction, Loading dictionaries, Message Translation, Indirect Message Translation and Plural Forms.
sources.confirmed: Boost.Locale uses GNU gettext catalogs and can return a delayed message object that resolves through a stream locale or an explicitly requested locale. Its examples compose translation with value formatting and let catalog rules choose plural forms.
sources.limits: Its C++ stream and locale interfaces would need an idiomatic Rust equivalent; applications still must manage catalogs, fallback behavior and formatting compatibility. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C20.json.

sources.title: ECMA-402 first-edition Intl service objects
sources.confirmed: The first edition is explicitly dated December 2012 and specifies an internationalization API complementary to the ECMAScript language specification. The contents distinguish Collator, NumberFormat and DateTimeFormat service objects.
sources.limits: The first edition covers collation, numbers and dates rather than full message translation, gender or plural grammar; it is a complementary standard API, not evidence that all internationalization belongs in an external package. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C20.json.

sources.title: Mozilla L20n localization language
sources.sections_read: Dated article body: strings as objects, gender selection and plural rules; comments and author profiles were not used.
sources.confirmed: The examples place gender and plural-selection logic inside localization files while the application requests a message by identifier. They describe translator-controlled behavior independent of the source language's grammar.
sources.limits: This introduces its own syntax, parser and translator tooling; the 2012 article establishes a design with examples, not deployment or demonstrated suitability for Rust. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C20.json.

sources.limits: The first edition covers collation, numbers and dates rather than full message translation, gender or plural grammar; it is a complementary standard API, not evidence that all internationalization belongs in an external package. sources.title: GNU gettext catalog selection followed by ordinary interpolation
sources.version_or_date: Live GNU gettext manual; exact version/publication date unverified
sources.sections_read: Direct unauthenticated HTTP GET; ngettext contract, formatting example, fallback behavior and PO header plural-selection rules.
sources.confirmed: The direct request succeeded with HTTP 200. The manual describes catalog-driven plural selection before printf interpolation, with plural rules stored in PO metadata and a two-form source-language fallback if no catalog is found.
sources.limits: The source fallback assumes singular/plural source messages and is not a complete system for arbitrary grammatical dependencies; Rust would still need a compatible runtime template formatter or generated adapter. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C20.json.

sources.title: Babel 1.3 catalog tooling and CLDR services
sources.version_or_date: Babel tag 1.3; official changelog dates this release to 2013-07-29
sources.sections_read: Direct unauthenticated HTTP GET; tagged introduction, Message Catalogs and Locale Data.
sources.confirmed: The version 1.3 documentation already describes the separation between gettext catalog tooling and CLDR-based locale services, including pluggable extraction methods. This verifies that the proposed architectural split is present in the dated historical version.
sources.limits: Babel is a Python package, so Rust would need a corresponding library or bridge; locale-aware value formatting and catalog tooling alone do not provide every whole-message grammatical feature. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C20.json.

sources.title: ICU MessageFormat, verified in ICU 52.1
sources.version_or_date: ICU tag release-52-1; official release page dates 52.1 to 2013-10-09
sources.sections_read: Direct unauthenticated HTTP GET; public MessageFormat class, constructors, pattern grammar and ICU/JDK differences.
sources.confirmed: The release-52-1 source includes named and numbered arguments, plural/select/selectordinal pattern branches, locale-bearing constructors, and examples whose message patterns come from resources. This confirms an actual historical library implementation rather than only a current guide.
sources.limits: Rust would need a binding or implementation, message-resource handling and maintained locale data; the historical source is not a ready Rust package, and its existence does not prove a migration would be useful. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C20.json.
